items.entity: design domain of Fig. 5 (width x height)
items.description: Sec. 3.1 refers to 'the design domain in Figure 5', meshed with 200 x 200 bilinear quads. Its physical width, height and aspect ratio are never stated in the text. The load width (0.04) and passive-pad width (0.025) are absolute lengths, so the domain size fixes how big they are relative to the domain. A 1 x 1 square (dx = 0.005) makes both whole numbers of elements and is the most likely reading.
readings: 1 x 1 unit square (dx = 0.005; 0.04 load = 8 elements, 0.025 pad = 5 elements)
2 x 2 square (dx = 0.01; load = 4 elements, pad = 2.5 elements)
0.5 x 0.5 square (dx = 0.0025; load = 16 elements, pad = 10 elements)
non-square rectangle (e.g. 2 x 1) meshed with 200 x 200 non-square elements

items.entity: vertical (u_y) restraints at 'the center nodes on each side'
items.description: Sec. 3.1: 'The center nodes on each side of the domain are restricted against vertical displacements.' 'Each side' can mean only the two loaded (left/right) edges or all four edges. 'Center nodes' can mean one mid-edge node or the group of central nodes under the load. Fixing the domain's centre node horizontally is clear. With only left/right restraints the supports are statically determinate and carry no reaction under the self-equilibrated loads; the other readings add redundant restraints that may or may not affect the pure-compliance optimum.
readings: u_y = 0 only at the mid-height node of the left edge and of the right edge (plus u_x = 0 at the domain centre node)
u_y = 0 at the mid-edge node of all four edges (left, right, top, bottom) plus u_x = 0 at the centre node
u_y = 0 at all nodes of the loaded segments (y = 0.48-0.52 on a unit square) on the left and right edges, plus u_x = 0 at the centre node

items.entity: the two inward horizontal loads on the left/right edges
items.description: Sec. 3.1: 'The widths of these loads are L_load = 0.04 with a magnitude of 10^-3 at each load.' The text does not say whether 10^-3 is the resultant force, a traction per unit length, or a per-node value. The reported omega = 0.5 compliances (~8.5e-6) fit a resultant of 1e-3 per load: an ideal straight bar of volume 0.15 gives F^2 L/(E A) ~ 6.7e-6.
readings: resultant force 1e-3 per load (uniform traction 1e-3/0.04 = 0.025 per unit length)
traction 1e-3 per unit length over 0.04 (resultant 4e-5 per load)
1e-3 applied at every node of the loaded segment (resultant ~9e-3 per load with 9 nodes)

items.entity: distribution of each 0.04-wide load over the edge nodes
items.description: Sec. 3.1 calls them 'distributed loads' of width 0.04 'around the horizontal symmetry axis' but gives no load profile or nodal lumping scheme. The effect is mostly local because a passive solid pad sits under each load.
readings: uniform traction over the 0.04 segment centred at mid-height, consistent lumping (end nodes half weight) over 9 nodes on a unit-square mesh
equal nodal forces on all 9 nodes of the segment

items.entity: passive solid pads at the two loads
items.description: Sec. 3.1: 'Passive solid regions are located at the loads with a width of 0.025.' Only one dimension is given. It is unclear whether 0.025 is the depth into the domain or the length along the edge, and what the other dimension is (perhaps the 0.04 load width). In the L-beam text (Sec. 3.2), 'width' means the along-edge size ('same width as the load and a height of 0.05').
readings: 0.025 deep (x) x 0.04 tall (y, = load width), centred at mid-height (5 x 8 elements on a unit-square mesh)
0.025 x 0.025 square centred on the load (5 x 5 elements), narrower than the load
0.025 along the edge (y) x 0.04 deep (x), reading 'width' as the along-edge size as in the L-beam text

items.entity: volume constraint V_b* = 0.15: treatment of passive pads
items.description: Eq. (19) normalises the volume by V_Omega (total volume), with V_b* = 0.15 on the blueprint design. It does not say whether the passive solid pads count toward the material volume or the reference volume. On a unit square the pads are about 0.002, roughly 1.3% of the material budget.
readings: 0.15 of the full domain area, pads counted as solid (rho = 1) in the material sum
0.15 of the full domain area, pads excluded from the material sum
0.15 of the non-passive design area only

items.entity: stiffness interpolation / which omega = 1 run to reproduce
items.description: Sec. 3.1 solves the pure-compliance case three ways: SIMP (singlescale), HS (Hashin-Shtrikman upper bound, Eq. 8, on rho = x~ * s~bar) and HS-S (HS plus a local-buckling stress constraint, started from the SIMP design). Fig. 8 text says SIMP and HS give similar but not identical designs. HS-S needs buckling eigenvalues, the KS parameter P, the mode-set size and the p-norm exponent, none of which are given anywhere.
readings: SIMP singlescale run (natural choice for a single-material solver)
HS interpolation (Eq. 8) with no stress constraint
HS-S (not reproducible on a linear minimum-compliance solver)

items.entity: SIMP penalisation (and Emin) for the singlescale run
items.description: Sec. 3.1 says the SIMP run was 'performed using the code from [18]' but gives no penalisation exponent. p = 3 appears only in the Fig. 1(a) comparison. Emin = 1e-6 E0 is stated only for the HS void.
readings: p = 3 fixed, Emin = 1e-6 E0
p continuation (e.g. 1 -> 3), Emin = 1e-6 E0
p = 3 with Emin = 1e-9 E0

items.entity: filter radius / projected field for a single-density-field implementation
items.description: Sec. 2.1 uses two fields. The density x is filtered with R_x = 1.5 dx and not projected. The void indicator s is filtered with R_s = 4.5 dx and projected (eta = 0.5 +/- 0.25 in Sec. 3.1, beta 2 -> 256). The SIMP run used the code of [18], and the text does not say whether it used this two-field scheme or one filtered-and-projected density field, or which radius applied. A single-field solver has to pick one.
readings: single density field, filter R = 1.5 dx, robust Heaviside projection of the filtered density (eta = 0.25/0.5/0.75)
single density field, filter R = 4.5 dx, robust projection (eta = 0.25/0.5/0.75)
two-field scheme rho = x~(R = 1.5 dx) * H_eta(s~(R = 4.5 dx)) with SIMP applied to rho

items.entity: lower bound x_min on the density field
items.description: Eq. (19) contains x_min <= x_j <= 1, but a value (0.27) is given only for the L-beam in Sec. 3.2. No value is given for the uniaxial compression example.
readings: x_min = 0 (or tiny, void handled by Emin)
x_min = 0.1 (lowest characterised microstructure density)
x_min = 0.27 (L-beam value)

items.entity: robust formulation: update of dilated volume bound V_d*
items.description: Sec. 2: the volume constraint acts on the dilated design, and V_d* is 'continuously updated' so the blueprint meets V_b* = 0.15. The update rule and frequency are not given.
readings: rescale V_d* every iteration so the blueprint volume equals 0.15
update V_d* every ~20 iterations
non-robust solver: impose 0.15 directly on the blueprint (eta = 0.5) design

items.entity: normalisation C_0 in the robust max objective (omega = 1)
items.description: Eq. (19) with omega = 1 gives the objective max_m C(rho^m)/C_0, where C_0 is the value 'for the initial design'. It is unclear whether one C_0 serves the eroded, blueprint and dilated designs or each realisation has its own (Eq. 1 defines J^KS_0 per rho^m). Per-realisation values change which realisation drives the min-max.
readings: one common C_0 for all realisations (the max is then the largest raw compliance, normally the eroded design)
realisation-specific C_0^m (each design normalised by its own initial compliance)

items.entity: initial design for the first omega = 1 runs
items.description: Sec. 3.1 says later omega steps restart from the previous design and HS-S starts from the SIMP designs, but gives no starting guess for the first omega = 1 runs. Sec. 3.2, by contrast, says its designs start from uniform guesses.
readings: uniform density 0.15 (single field), or x = 0.15 with s = 1
x = 1 with uniform s = 0.15
uniform x = s = 0.5

items.description: Sec. 3 gives the beta schedule: beta = 2 for 125 iterations, then doubled every 75 iterations, reaching 256 at about iteration 576. No stopping rule or maximum iteration count is given.
readings: stop at a fixed count shortly after beta = 256 is reached (e.g. 650 iterations)
stop when the maximum design change falls below a tolerance (e.g. 0.01) at beta = 256
fixed large budget (e.g. 1000 iterations)

items.description: Sec. 3.1: the design is 'forced to be symmetric around the horizontal and vertical center axes', while the analysis uses the full model. The text does not say how symmetry is imposed.
readings: quarter-domain design variables mirrored to the full mesh before filtering
full-domain variables with mirrored variables/sensitivities averaged each iteration
symmetry imposed only on the filtered/projected physical fields

items.description: MMA is named (Sec. 2.2.3, App. B), but move limits and asymptote parameters are not given. The optimizer settings of the code of [18], used for the SIMP run, are not restated.
readings: default MMA settings (Svanberg)
move limit 0.2
move limit 0.1

items.description: No plane-stress/plane-strain assumption or thickness is stated. kappa0 = E0/(2(1-nu0)) in Sec. 2.1 is the plane-stress 2D bulk modulus, which suggests plane stress. Thickness only scales compliance.
readings: plane stress, unit thickness
plane strain, unit thickness
plane stress, non-unit thickness t (compliance scales as 1/t)
